CORAM : DR. SHALINI PHANSALKAR-JOSHI, J.
 DATE : 6TH JANUARY 2016.

ORAL JUDGMENT: [PER: DR. SHALINI PHANSALKAR-JOSHI, J.]
1.

The State has preferred this appeal challenging the judgment and order dated 27th February,
2002, of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Pali, District: Raigad, in R.C.C. No.9 of 1996, thereby acquitting 919 APEAL 813 OF 2002.doc respondent, for the offence punishable under Section 7(i)
read with 2(ia),
(a), 2(ia) (m) and Section 7(v) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to as,
"the Act"), read with Rule 50 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, read with Rule 5 of Maharashtra Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules 1962, punishable under Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and rules thereunder.

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts of the appeal can be stated as follows :-
On 13th September, 1995 at about 8.30 a.m., P.W.1 Food Inspector Shri. S. H. Joshi,
intervened the respondent and enquired with him about the contents in the cans which he was carrying.
Respondent disclosed that the cans contain buffalo milk and he was carrying the same for selling it to the customers.

P.W.1 Food Inspector Joshi,
disclosed his identity and intimated respondent his intention of drawing sample of said milk for the purpose of analysis.
P.W.1 Food Inspector Joshi, then purchased 750 milliliter of buffalo milk from the can for Rs.6/- and divided it, into three bottles of equal quantity.
He added 20 drops formalin in each bottle as preservative of milk.
The bottles were corked tightly and sealed in the presence of panchas.
Then requisite formalities of issuing notices in form VI and under Section 14(a) of the Act, were completed.
One of 919 APEAL 813 OF 2002.doc the sample bottles, was sent to Local Heal Authority; whereas one was sent to Public Analyst.

The report of Public Analyst,
disclosed that the sample was not conforming to the standard of buffalo milk, as laid down in the Rules under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
Hence all the papers were sent to the Joint Commissioner, Konkan Division, Food and Drug Administration on 26.10.1995, for necessary sanction.

On receipt of the sanction,
P.W.1 Food Inspector Shri. Joshi, filed private criminal case against respondent, for the various offences, as noted above, for selling adulterated buffalo milk and selling it The State Of Maharashtra vs Shantaram Narayan Chile on 6 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134760377/
2 without having any licence.

sentences.text: 3. On the receipt of summons, respondent appeared and pleaded not guilty.
In the trial Court, P.W.1 examined himself and two panchas viz P.W.2 Babaji Arekar, P.W.3 Gopal Bhat.
Both of them did not support the case.
Prosecution also led evidence of Senior Clerk of Local Health Authority P.W.4 Shrinivas Kulkarni and then closed its case.

4. On appreciation of their evidence, the trial Court was pleased to acquit respondent of all the charges levelled against him, mainly, on the ground that there is no proper compliance of the Rules and Regulations laid down under the Act, for drawing of the sample.
919 APEAL 813 OF 2002.doc 5.

This judgment of the trial Court is challenged in this appeal by learned APP by submitting that despite sufficient incriminating evidence available on record, trial Court has committed an error in acquitting the respondent of the charges levelled against him and hence the impugned judgment is required to be quashed and set aside.

6. However, in my considered opinion, this submission is devoid of any substance as cross examination of P.W.1 S.H. Joshi - Food Inspector, who is the only material witness available in the case, who has supported prosecution, reveals that there is total non compliance of the requisite formalities,for drawing of the sample.
There is absolutely no corroborating evidence on record to the effect that P.W.1 Shri Joshi has drawn said sample on the date and time mentioned by him.
Both the panchas to the panchnama of drawing of the sample are declared hostile and have not supported the prosecution case.
Though learned APP has cross examined them nothing worthwhile is elicited in their cross examination to support the evidence of P.W.1 Food Inspector Shri. Joshi.
7. In his cross examination, P.W.1 Shri.Joshi has also admitted that respondent was found carrying total 8 cans of the milk.
However, how the sample was drawn is not mentioned in the panchnama or in his 919 APEAL 813 OF 2002.doc evidence before the Court.
Whether sample was collected from one can or from each of the 8 cans is not at all made clear.
Conversely, he has admitted that there is no whisper in the panchnama as to what method or procedure was followed for drawing of the sample.
Further there is also no mention in the panchnama as to what level sample was poured in the glass bottle.
It is not proved whether the sample was homogeneous one mixing it properly after being collected from different cans or whether it was collected from one of the cans.
It is not mentioned in the panchnama as to whether sample bottles were clean, dry and as to who has cleaned those bottles.
8. Moreover, Public Analyst is not examined to prove which method was adopted for analysis of the sample.

Merely because sample was not conforming to the standard of buffalo milk, as laid down in the Rules framed under the Act, is not sufficient, but it must be shown as to how it was not conforming and what was the reason for not conforming.

In the absence of evidence of Public Analyst to that effect and the details thereof being not noted in the report Exh.39, nor it is stated as to which tests were conducted to know whether the sample was conforming to the standard as laid The State Of Maharashtra vs Shantaram Narayan Chile on 6 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134760377/

Hence, in my considered opinion, trial Court was justified in giving benefit of doubt to the respondent and acquitting him of the charges levelled against him.
Therefore, no interference is warranted in the impugned judgment of the trial Court.
The appeal, thus, is dismissed and the bail bond of the Respondent stands cancelled.
